title: Self-Attention: Q, K, V
interviewAnswer: Self-attention lets each token build a context-dependent representation by comparing its query with other tokens’ keys and taking a weighted combination of their values.
why: Attention is the central operation behind modern transformers and many multimodal/generative systems.
intuition: Think of each token asking a question (query), advertising what it contains (key), and carrying information to share (value). Query–key similarity determines how much of each value is mixed into the output.
deepDive: For matrices Q, K and V, scaled dot-product attention computes QKᵀ/√d, applies softmax row-wise, and multiplies by V. Multiple heads learn different projection subspaces. Causal language models additionally mask future positions.
code:
import torch
scores = Q @ K.transpose(-2, -1) / (Q.size(-1) ** 0.5)
weights = scores.softmax(dim=-1)
out = weights @ V
commonMistakes: Saying attention “finds the most important word” as if it were one fixed interpretation.
Forgetting the √d scaling or causal mask.
Assuming attention weights are guaranteed explanations.
followUps: Why is attention O(n²) in sequence length?
production: Long contexts create memory/latency pressure; serving systems use KV caches, efficient attention kernels and sometimes alternative architectures.
workedExample: In a sentence, the representation of “bank” can attend differently to “river” versus “loan”, producing context-dependent meaning.

lab.goal: Implement scaled dot-product self-attention with explicit tensor shapes.
lab.buildIt:
import torch, math
B,T,D=2,4,8
x=torch.randn(B,T,D); Wq=torch.randn(D,D); Wk=torch.randn(D,D); Wv=torch.randn(D,D)
Q,K,V=x@Wq,x@Wk,x@Wv
scores=Q@K.transpose(-2,-1)/math.sqrt(D)
weights=scores.softmax(-1); out=weights@V
print(Q.shape,scores.shape,out.shape)
lab.useIt:
from torch.nn.functional import scaled_dot_product_attention
out2=scaled_dot_product_attention(Q,K,V)
print(out2.shape)
